cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Database performance is latency (how long one query takes, tracked as p50, p95, p99) and throughput (queries or transactions per second), limited by whichever resource is the bottleneck.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Bottlenecks: query efficiency and indexes, CPU, memory and cache hit ratio, disk IOPS, connections and locks. Measure first with the slow query log, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, percentiles and resource metrics, then fix the real bottleneck with indexes, query changes, caching, pooling, replicas or scaling, and re-measure.

questions.q: Will a bigger instance fix a slow database?
questions.a: Only if hardware is the bottleneck. A missing index still scans the whole table, just slightly faster.
Latency is time per query; throughput is queries or transactions per second.
